$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `cost-monitoring`'s canonical store,
the THIRD owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM.
One entry per guard: per scope predicate, per conditional-write precondition,
per statement the port's contract says must be one statement, per property
only hand-written SQL can express, and per shape check that stands where a
migration-only CHECK stands. Each carries the file it lives in, the EXACT
text that implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the
NAMED cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A FIFTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json and mutations-outbox.json rather than an extension of
any of them, for the reason the fourth was: five tranches are five separate
claims about five separate port surfaces, and a reader checking one should
not have to read past the other four. All five are hashed by the same
packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. Two of the six rows are IMMUTABLE —
the database revokes UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on `BudgetThresholdEvent`
and on `AlertDeliveryRetry` — so a defect written into either cannot be
corrected afterwards. And the port's two hardest promises are both about
what does NOT happen: `claimDelivery` must be ONE conditional write (a read
then a write sends the alert twice) and `insertThresholdEvent` must surface a
duplicate as `null` rather than as an error (an error sends it twice too, or
aborts the transaction the fan-out is in). Neither is visible in a returned
value on a store with one caller, which is exactly the shape of guard a
green suite hides.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep
unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies a run
with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
A SECOND SWEEP WIDENED SIX ENTRIES, AND THE SEVENTH SUITE IS ITS RESULT.
Re-running all forty scored SIX of them with zero executed cases -- M-C06,
M-C13, M-C15, M-C17, M-C18 and M-C20. None was a module-load failure: each
edit compiled and collected, and then broke `cost-conformance.integration.
test.ts` while it was BUILDING its transcript, in a `beforeAll`, so vitest
reported every case in the file SKIPPED and no named case went red. A suite
set that turns red only through a setup crash names no promise, and it is the
same signal a cleaned `dist` produces, so the driver scored all six VACUOUS
rather than counting them as kills.
Widening the sweep to the WHOLE cost suite set found a named case for two of
them already in the tree -- M-C15 in the statement-count suite and M-C18 in
the transaction suite -- and none at all for the other four. Those four are
why `cost-idempotency.integration.test.ts` exists: one named case each for the
insert form that does not raise, the uuid shape test the vault's question
depends on, the terminal status that stops a second send, and the count test
that keeps a stale dispatcher's send record out of the history. All six now
name the suite that carries their case rather than the conformance run, and
all forty are KILLED by a NAMED case with none vacuous.
THE NEW SUITE'S OWN FIXTURE WAS REFUSED BY A GUARD ON ITS FIRST RUN.
`requireRetryRecord` (M-C35) rejected a SUCCEEDED send record that still
carried `upstream_500`, which is the guard doing exactly what its entry
claims for it.
That failure mode was LIVE on this branch and is what the fifth commit
closed: the `postgres-tenancy-repository` CI job built `tenancy` and
`identity-access` and not `cost-monitoring`, and these six suites resolve
that context through two published subpaths, both of which are `dist/`. The
classifier earned its keep a second time in this sweep, on M-C14's first
form: the edit left unbalanced parentheses, the module did not load, and the
run was scored VACUOUS rather than as forty-one kills.
For one entry: replace its `from` with its `to` in the named file (the driver
requires the `from` to occur EXACTLY ONCE, so a stale entry is an error and
not a silent no-op), run the named suites against a real PostgreSQL
container, and confirm a NAMED case in `kills` is among the failures. Then
revert and confirm green again.
ALL FORTY ARE RUN AGAINST A REAL POSTGRESQL. Three of them -- M-C25, M-C37
and M-C38 -- are ALSO killed by `cost-rows.test.ts`, the one suite of the seven
that `pnpm test:v1-packages` runs; every other entry is about something only
the database can answer: which rows a predicate matched, whether two
statements rolled back together, whether a claim was refused while a lease
was live, how many statements a read cost, and whether a CHECK a migration
added agrees with the guard that restates it.
FOUR FINDINGS CAME OUT OF WRITING THIS SWEEP and are recorded in the entries
themselves rather than only here.
1. `insertBudget`, `insertAlertChannel` and both delivery inserts use
`createMany` + `skipDuplicates` -- `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` -- rather
than `create`, because on PostgreSQL a raised constraint ABORTS the
caller's whole transaction and the port's callers keep writing in it
2. `countChannelsUsingCredential` must refuse a non-uuid reference in
JavaScript, because sending it to a `@db.Uuid` comparison raises 22P02
and turns a question with an answer into a driver error (M-C13).
3. `claimDelivery`'s predicate is deliberately SCALAR-ONLY: the tenant
chain is a relation filter everywhere else in that file, and on the
claim it would be a subquery the connector may satisfy with a second
statement -- which would make the claim a read and a write again
(M-C40, measured rather than argued).
4. A STORE IN THIS PACKAGE CANNOT WRITE OUTSIDE THE CALLER'S TRANSACTION,
and that is why M-C14 and M-C21 are shaped the way they are.
`TenancyTransactions` exposes `writer`, `reader` and `atomic` and
nothing else; `reader()` returns the ambient frame's client when one is
open, and `atomic` resolves through `unitOfWork.run`, which JOINS an
open frame. Both escapes were tried and both left every case green,
because neither is reachable. Atomicity is a property of the seam and
is falsified in mutations-ports.json where the seam lives; what these
two entries falsify is that the second write is ISSUED, which is what
lets the failure injection reach the first.
FOUR SUITES WERE WIDENED BECAUSE A GUARD SURVIVED, and the widenings added no
test case at all -- each is an assertion or an observation inside a case that
already existed, which is why the census did not move:
M-C10  `updateAlertChannel`'s `deletedAt: null` term had nothing that could
turn red: the tombstone case exercised the two READS and no write.
It now edits the tombstoned channel and requires the refusal.
M-C13  every credential the conformance scenario named was a well-formed
uuid, including the deliberately-missing one, so the guard that
refuses a malformed reference was unreachable. The scenario now
asks with `not-a-uuid`.
M-C24  the two crossing identifiers were numbered in deadline order, so
the outer `ORDER BY picked."dueAt"` and the id tie-break agreed and
removing the former changed nothing. They are now numbered against
the deadline order.
M-C38  the constraints suite plants an OBJECT threshold, which the type
test refuses before the whole-number test is reached, so only the
pure suite's non-whole NUMBER can see that mutation. The entry
claims only the case that was seen to go red.

kills: a cap, read from its columns a period this binary has no arithmetic for is refused, not defaulted
identifiers, limits and thresholds on a cap a period this binary has no arithmetic for is refused on the way OUT

mutations.name: M-C38 rows: the thresholds column's ELEMENTS are read exactly
mutations.note: The JSON root check guarantees an array and says nothing about the elements, so a row written by a migration or by hand can hold `[50, "80", null]` and satisfy every constraint the table has. Reading that as `[50, NaN, 0]` fires a cap at a percentage no operator asked for. The constraints suite plants `[{ percent: 50 }]` -- an OBJECT -- so it is refused on the type test and cannot see this mutation; only the pure suite's non-whole NUMBER reaches it, and only that case is claimed as the kill.
kills: a cap, read from its columns thresholds that are not whole numbers are refused, not coerced

mutations.name: M-C39 budgets: a page and its total are ONE read, not two
mutations.note: A separate count is a second statement AND a second snapshot: the page and the total rendered beside it would then be able to disagree about which rows exist. The pin is per read and holds over a 3-cap and a 30-cap environment, so this is caught by the COUNT rather than by any returned value.
kills: every read costs the same over a small environment and a large one each read's statement count matches its pin, over BOTH sizes
